search_log: Searched "The Knight and the Moth" Rachel Gillig excerpt first chapter; found and opened Orbit/Hachette's authorized Chapter One extract.
Searched the title with publisher-domain and excerpt terms; found and opened a separate Hachette interior scene with sustained first-person narration.
Searched the title with "first person," "POV," "narrator," "single POV," and "Sybil's POV"; opened explicit completed-book descriptions identifying a single first-person Sybil/Six narrator.

Searched the exact phrase "You know this story, Bartholomew" to investigate whether the apparent address signaled a separate narrator; results associated it with the book's recurring Bartholomew address and revealed no autonomous contrary-person section.

Searches for alternating, dual, frame, diary, and epistolary narration produced no credible evidence that this volume contains sustained base sections in another grammatical person; unrelated search snippets about other books or the sequel were disregarded.
person_note: The Goodreads material repeatedly exposes a participating narrator through 'I,' 'me,' and 'my,' including narration beats embedded in dialogue-heavy quotations. The address to Bartholomew is consistent with that first-person teller's constitutive storytelling frame, not evidence of a separate second-person base. Authorized publisher excerpts independently show the same first-person voice in the opening and an interior scene, while completed-book reviews explicitly identify a single Sybil/Six first-person viewpoint. Speech, aphorisms, universal 'you/we,' and the dedication were excluded from person inference. No credible evidence of sustained narration in another person was found.
